correctness.rationale: A stationary two-sided Poisson construction and coupling establish a unique invariant process. Five exact generator equations solve the stationary second and fourth moments. The mixed moment loses mass at R+Q-c because the common clock acts only once. An independent two-time Poisson-survival integral verifies the fourth moment; positive differentiation and feasible nonnegative rates prove sharpness and the unique inverse. A standalone SymPy/mpmath checker passed 680 integral/rational checks plus exact generator identities; numerical tests are not used as infinite proofs. The generator identities Lx=-R x, Lomega=-Q omega, and stationary E[x omega]=0 separately prove the entire lagged covariance matrix is diagonal and independent of clock overlap at fixed marginal rates.

value.rationale: A natural open selective-resetting extension of the 2022 stochastic-diffusivity model raises whether reset coordination can be recovered when marginal reset rates and second moments agree. The sharp complete interval of stationary kurtosis values and its exact inverse solve that identifiability problem; synchronized versus independent resetting doubles the fourth moment at identical marginal variance. This is a physically meaningful structural distinction rather than an arbitrary parameter slice, while inference precision from finite samples remains open. The stronger conclusion holds even if all two-time second-order data of both physical variables are measured; kurtosis supplies the first demonstrated separating statistic.
